description:
You are a quantitative analyst at a trading firm. A colleague implemented a Python library of technical indicators (EMA, RSI, Sharpe ratio, max drawdown) that is used by the backtesting system. The library is producing incorrect trading signals — the CI pipeline is failing and the risk desk has flagged that computed Sharpe ratios and RSI values are wildly off from Bloomberg terminal benchmarks.

The project is already open in PyCharm at /home/ga/PycharmProjects/trading_indicators.

Your task:
1. Run the test suite to understand which indicators are computing incorrectly
2. Identify and fix all mathematical bugs in the indicator implementations
3. Ensure all tests pass after your fixes

Do NOT change the function signatures, test file, or the input data. Only fix the implementation logic.

Run tests with: python -m pytest tests/ -v

bug_locations: indicators/rsi.py:relative_strength_index (wrong RS formula — uses subtraction not division)
indicators/stats.py:sharpe_ratio (divides by variance instead of std dev)
indicators/stats.py:max_drawdown (computes wrong running max — uses cummax not rolling peak from start)
metadata.industry: Securities, Commodity Contracts, and Other Financial Investments
